title: observability: propagate request-id & traceparent across API surface; structured logs + per-endpoint metric tags
author: Aisha Patel
commits: feat(gateway): add X-Request-ID middleware and upstream propagation
feat(trace): accept and propagate traceparent; wire into tracer context
feat(logging): structured log fields for api.request_id trace.id trace.span
feat(metrics): attach route/model/method tags to per-endpoint metrics
fix(openai-compat): include request-id/trace headers in streaming chunks and event frames
test: integration tests for trace & request-id propagation; update CI matrix
description:
Motivation: customers and internal operators need consistent correlation across the API surface (hosted API, OpenAI compatibility layer, SDKs, and internal downstream services) to debug production incidents and link traces/metrics/logs. This PR implements request-id propagation, W3C traceparent support, structured log fields, and per-endpoint metric tags. It also includes small compatibility updates to the OpenAI-compat streaming layer so streamed chunks surface the same correlation headers.

What changed (high level):
- Gateway: new middleware that sets/forwards X-Request-ID (prefer incoming header, otherwise generate deterministic UUIDv4) and injects into context.
- Tracing: accept W3C traceparent header, convert into internal tracer context and propagate to downstream calls and internal runtime components.
- Logging: structured logger now includes api.request_id, trace.id, and trace.span in JSON logs emitted from the API path. Backwards format remains supported.
- Metrics: per-endpoint tags (api.route, api.model, api.method) are attached to request-level counters/histograms so dashboards can break down by route and model. Low-cardinality enforcement applied (route+model only).
- OpenAI-compat: streaming handler now includes x-request-id and traceparent in transport frames where appropriate so client-side logs can correlate stream events to server traces. Also fixed a race where stream headers were not set on reconnect.
- SDK: Python OpenAI-compat client surfaces request_id on Response objects (response.request_id) and preserves trace headers on streaming iterators.
- Tests: integration tests for header propagation and CI acceptance tests added.

Checklist:
- [x] Gateway middleware implemented and unit tested
- [x] Tracing propagation wired and integration-tested with tracer shim
- [x] Structured log fields added and validated against console ingestion
- [x] Per-endpoint metric tags implemented with low-cardinality guardrails
- [x] OpenAI-compat streaming update and race fix
- [x] SDK change and docs updated
- [x] Added integration tests and updated CI to run them

Backward compatibility and rollout:
- Headers are additive; existing clients continue to work. If callers send their own X-Request-ID/traceparent we preserve them.
- Structured logs add new fields; logging ingestion pipelines should handle unknown fields safely.
- Metrics tags are low-cardinality; we validated against historical route/model distributions.
- Rollout plan: feature-flagged on gateway and gradual rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with a kill switch. Documentation and console dashboard updated before full rollout.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests for middleware, propagation, logger formatting added.
- Integration test deploys a small echo service and asserts request-id + traceparent reach downstream and are present in traces/metrics/logs.
- Manual QA: exercised streaming client to ensure request-id appears on stream events and reconnects keep same trace context where expected.

Notes for reviewers:
- Look at the gateway middleware contract: we intentionally normalize header name to X-Request-ID for consistency with existing logs.
- The traceparent handling uses our tracer shim so that vendor-specific trace context is preserved in the enrichers.
- Metrics tag cardinality enforcement lives in go/metrics/route_tags.go; please confirm the whitelist is sensible.

Related work: ENG-2145 (observability runway), ENG-2190 (openai-compat stability), PM-342 (customer ask: correlated logs/traces).

Aisha Patel (author): Implemented coalescing and added unit tests asserting label values. Kept code path configurable behind env var for experiments.
Sofia Ramirez: OpenAI-compat streaming change looks safe; please add a note to the migration docs for third-party integrators.

release_notes: Added API correlation headers (X-Request-ID, traceparent) across gateway, OpenAI-compat streaming, structured JSON log fields (api.request_id, trace.id), and per-endpoint metric tags (api.route, api.model). Backward compatible; rollout behind flag.
